title: OneFlow reinserts products with the right timing
summary: At various points in the post deboning process, operators reinsert products onto the conveyor belt at random after completing their manual tasks. This creates a risk of product overlap when singulated products are required. With JBT Marel OneFlow, suitable for use with AMF-i, trimming stations and SensorX, the product flow on the belt can be kept consistent. It ensures individual processing downstream and minimizes rejects. Not in the least, OneFlow has considerable ergonomical advantages for the operators.
body_markdown:
#### Organize the flow


In today’s secondary processing lines, from deboning to packing, many operators still perform manual tasks. After their interventions, product flow on the belt can quickly become chaotic, as there is no way to organize items consistently.
But now, there’s OneFlow. Birgir Freyr Ragnarsson continues, “OneFlow finds the ideal moment to reinsert a product on the conveyor belt. At multiple manual handling points in the post deboning process, it can ensure consistent, singulated product flow. Most of the time, OneFlow will be combined with trimming.”


#### Buffer and release


The ‘dropper’, a product holding hopper above the belt, is the key component of OneFlow, acting as a buffer and release bin. Operators place their treated products into this dropper. By tracking the position of each meat piece on the belt, OneFlow’s software precisely detects when there’s an empty space available for an additional item. It keeps the product in the dropper, buffering it until the optimal moment for release, which ensures the integration with the flow on the belt. OneFlow not only singulates the product flow but also positions the products accurately on the belt, long side leading. OneFlow therefore precisely organizes the infeed for downstream processes. Up to 120 fillets per minute can be handled, all the time maintaining a consistent flow. The reduced manual handling also benefits food safety.
